title: Did you know…
paragraphs:
Peter saw the empty tomb.
Peter heard the testimony.
Peter ran to the evidence.
And then… he went back to fishing.
“Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing.” (John 21:3)

The smell of salt.
The creak of wood.
The familiar rhythm of casting nets.

This is where Peter feels safe.
This is where failure doesn’t follow him like a shadow.
Because something happened before this moment…

He denied Jesus.
Not once.
Not twice.
Three times.

You can encounter Jesus…
and still drift back to what you were before.

Not because He failed you—
but because shame convinces you that you failed Him beyond repair.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Peter didn’t just go fishing for food.
He went fishing to escape identity.

“I’m not a disciple anymore.”
“I’m not worthy of calling.”
“I’ll go back to who I was.”

You’ve seen God move.
You’ve felt conviction.
You’ve heard truth.

Back to the habit.
Back to the sin.
Back to the old mindset.

Because guilt is loud.
But grace feels distant—until it speaks.

Because when God has called you forward,
going backward becomes empty.
At dawn… a voice from the shore:

Not angry.
Not distant.
Not done with Peter.

The risen Son of God…
prepares a meal for the man who denied Him.
“Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me?” (John 21:17)

Grace doesn’t ignore your failure.
It redeems it.
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us…” — 1 John 1:9
“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus…” — Romans 8:1

Stay in the boat…
or come back to the shore where Jesus is calling your name.

Peter went from fisherman…
to failure…
to restored leader.

And what Jesus did for him—
He is still doing today.

Will you keep fishing in emptiness?
Or will you answer the voice on the shore?
